I01.label: Extra-Qurʾānic authority
I01.scope: Locate authorial arguments about whether Sunna can establish binding requirements beyond the Qurʾān's wording. Separate source authority from report authenticity, interpretation, and specification of general wording.

I02.label: Report sufficiency
I02.scope: Locate methodological or case-specific treatment of reports with limited routes. Separate narrator reliability, corroboration, public practice, legal domains, and epistemic versus practical effect.

I03.label: Report and general textual principle
I03.scope: Find discussions of an apparent report/text-principle conflict. Record whether the text is accepted, interpreted, specified, qualified, or rejected and the authorial reason; avoid reducing all conflicts to one rule.

I04.label: Communal practice and report
I04.scope: Locate direct treatment of transmitted or communal practice in relation to reports. Distinguish a named city's practice, inherited practice, consensus, and an author's report of another authority.

I05.label: Binding consensus
I05.scope: Locate definitions and evidentiary claims about binding consensus. Preserve who is said to agree, the generation/population, how agreement is known, and whether the passage is the author's claim or a report.

I06.label: Silence and consensus
terms: قول الصحابي لا يعرف له مخالف
I06.scope: Locate arguments about whether silence or lack of a recorded objection establishes agreement. Separate actual knowledge and opportunity to object from missing documentation.

I07.label: Analogy (qiyās)
I07.scope: Locate explicit argument about analogical extension, its conditions, and domains. Distinguish qiyās from interpreting general wording, identifying facts, and other forms of reasoning.

I08.label: Analogy in ritual requirements
I08.scope: Find direct positions or cases about analogical extension in worship. Separate worship whose rationale is treated as knowable from fixed quantities and prescribed forms; do not infer a blanket rule from a single example.

I09.label: Reason and binding judgment
I09.scope: Locate methodological claims about reason's role in obligation, prohibition, and moral evaluation. Distinguish moral intelligibility, factual harm assessment, and a binding revealed legal ruling.

I10.label: Public welfare in transactions
I10.scope: Locate arguments about welfare or harm in rulemaking, especially transactions. Preserve the source's terminology, whether it is an independent proof or a supporting consideration, and stated limits.

I11.label: Custom and unstated contract terms
I11.scope: Locate cases where custom supplies an unstated contract term or determines wording. Distinguish custom used to interpret language from custom that independently creates obligations.

I12.label: Custom and adequate fulfillment
I12.scope: Locate bounded examples where customary practice affects what counts as adequate performance or fulfillment. Record the obligation, domain, relevant community/time, and any textual or contractual constraints.

I13.label: Changed condition and application
I13.scope: Locate direct accounts of the relationship between an operative condition/cause and a ruling's application. Separate disappearance of a legally identified cause from changed facts or changed policy.

I14.label: Layperson and authorities
I14.scope: Locate direct statements about non-specialists seeking and following legal advice. Identify whether the passage concerns duty, competence, choosing among authorities, or a particular historical debate.

I15.label: Qualified jurist and inherited position
I15.scope: Locate bounded statements or cases about qualified jurists revising or departing from inherited positions. Distinguish an author's own reasoning from reporting school doctrine or a later rule about competence.

I16.label: Default status under uncertainty
terms: كل شيء حلال إلا ما فصل تحريمه
الأصل أن كل شيء مباح حتى يأتي تحريمه
كل شيء مباح حتى يأتي تحريمه
كل شيء حلال حتى يرد تحريمه
لا يحرم إلا ما حرم الله
I16.scope: Locate statements about the default status of ordinary activities or transactions when prohibition is not established. Separate that from worship, burdens of proof, precaution, and domain-specific exceptions.

I17.label: Uncertainty in ritual performance
I17.scope: Locate case rulings on uncertainty in worship, with the act, stage, evidence, and prescribed response stated. Treat prayer-unit doubt and tawaf/sa'i count as separate bounded subcases; do not merge their results into one undifferentiated precaution position. For Shamela 30130 preserve possible commentary and marginal-gloss layers separately; do not attribute an integrated passage to al-Ansari or al-Ramli until the edition and typography are checked. Shamela 30064 is a modern comparative compendium: use it to locate cases and cited sources only, and distinguish its editor's synthesis and quotations from primary authorial positions. For Shamela 2186, distinguish al-Shirazi's base text from al-Nawawi's commentary and verify the exact text layer and edition before attribution. Do not generalize one ritual case to all uncertainty or all obligations.

I18.label: Evidentiary uncertainty and punishment
I18.scope: Locate evidence and reasoning about uncertainty in fixed punishments. Distinguish authenticity of maxim reports, procedural proof, substantive doubt, and case-specific disagreement; do not turn one rule into a complete theory of punishment.

I19.label: Evidence for abrogation
I19.scope: Locate criteria for establishing abrogation between apparently different rulings. Preserve chronology, reconciliation, certainty of evidence, scope, and whether the text is methodological or case-specific.

I20.label: Supersession across source types
I20.scope: Locate explicit claims about whether one source type can supersede another. Keep source hierarchy, report transmission class, chronology, and abrogation evidence separate.
